parts.name: body shell

physics.Basic_description: The main white housing of the printer, featuring a smooth matte plastic finish and rounded corners.
physics.Functional_description: Encloses the internal printing mechanisms, electronics, and ink cartridges while providing structural integrity.
physics.Grasped_description: A robot gripper would grasp the sides or top edges of the shell to lift or reposition the entire printer.
physics.reason: Printer housings are injection-molded thin-walled shells enclosing air and components; treating as solid would vastly overestimate mass.

parts.description: The main white housing of the printer, featuring a smooth matte plastic finish and rounded corners.
parts.function: Encloses the internal printing mechanisms, electronics, and ink cartridges while providing structural integrity.

parts.name: output shadow

physics.Basic_description: A dark grey recessed area at the front bottom where paper exits, appearing as a shadowed cavity or textured surface.
physics.Functional_description: Defines the exit path for printed paper and protects the internal rollers from dust.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a graspable feature; it is a recessed cavity or surface detail.
physics.reason: This represents the inner wall or floor of the output slot, which is a thin plastic surface bounding an empty space.

parts.description: A dark grey recessed area at the front bottom where paper exits, appearing as a shadowed cavity or textured surface.
parts.function: Defines the exit path for printed paper and protects the internal rollers from dust.

parts.name: brand plate

physics.Basic_description: A small, rectangular blue-grey strip on the front left face, likely a logo or brand indicator.
physics.Functional_description: Displays the manufacturer's branding or model information.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flat to be grasped independently; part of the surface finish.
physics.reason: Likely a thin solid inlay or sticker applied to the surface, effectively solid in this context.

parts.description: A small, rectangular blue-grey strip on the front left face, likely a logo or brand indicator.

parts.name: badge roundel

physics.Basic_description: A small circular yellow/grey button or badge on the front right face.
physics.Functional_description: Likely a power button or status indicator light cover.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp; would be pressed with a fingertip or tool tip.
physics.reason: Small button caps are typically solid molded plastic pieces.

parts.description: A small circular yellow/grey button or badge on the front right face.

parts.name: top deck

physics.Basic_description: The flat, orange-tinted top surface of the printer, smooth and slightly curved at the edges.
physics.Functional_description: Serves as the top cover, often hinged to allow access to ink cartridges or paper jams.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper could press down on it to close, or grasp the edge to lift if it acts as a lid.
physics.reason: Top covers are large thin-walled plastic panels; modeling as solid would add kilograms of unrealistic mass.

parts.description: The flat, orange-tinted top surface of the printer, smooth and slightly curved at the edges.
parts.function: Serves as the top cover, often hinged to allow access to ink cartridges or paper jams.

parts.name: control panel

physics.Basic_description: The horizontal strip on the front face containing buttons and indicators, colored purple in the mask.
physics.Functional_description: Houses the user interface controls for operating the printer.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; interaction is limited to pressing buttons within it.
physics.reason: This is a faceplate or bezel, which is a thin shell covering the underlying PCB and switches.

parts.description: The horizontal strip on the front face containing buttons and indicators, colored purple in the mask.

parts.name: panel display

physics.Basic_description: A small cyan rectangular area on the control panel, representing an LCD screen or status light window.
physics.Functional_description: Displays printer status, error messages, or ink levels to the user.
physics.Grasped_description: Fragile and flat; not suitable for grasping.
physics.reason: Display windows are typically solid thin sheets of plastic or glass.

parts.description: A small cyan rectangular area on the control panel, representing an LCD screen or status light window.

parts.name: tray plate

physics.Basic_description: The magenta-colored flat plate extending from the front bottom, serving as the paper output tray.
physics.Functional_description: Catches and supports printed paper as it exits the printer.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper would grasp the front edge or side of this tray to extend or retract it.
physics.reason: Output trays are thin ribbed plastic structures; treating the bounding box as solid plastic would be too heavy.

parts.description: The magenta-colored flat plate extending from the front bottom, serving as the paper output tray.

parts.name: tray rail l

physics.Functional_description: Guides the extension and retraction of the output tray.
physics.Grasped_description: Too thin and recessed to be a primary grasp point.
physics.reason: Rails are often solid extruded or molded plastic rods/slats to provide stiffness.

parts.name: stopper flap

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
